title: On-demand remote dependency mounting and hermetic lint containers
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Problem: CI pipelines in the monorepo install the full dependency surface for every job and run linters inside ad-hoc images. This causes long cold-start times, high egress from package registries, and brittle lint environments that drift across teams. Proposal: introduce an on-demand remote dependency mounting mechanism (sparse dependency materialization backed by our CAS/remote-cache) and migrate linters to hermetic, small toolchain images pinned by digest. Goals: (1) avoid installing all transitive deps for unit tests and linters, (2) make lint environments reproducible across commits and runners, (3) reduce CI median job wall time by ~40% for language-specific pipelines, (4) cut registry egress and reduce flaky failures caused by dependency resolution. Approach: 1) Implement a lightweight dependency manifest extractor in bazel/gradle/npm flows that emits a minimal materialization manifest for each job. 2) Add a CI runner hook that mounts required dependency trees from our remote CAS using a FUSE-based sparse materializer or buildkit mount=type=cache augmented with remote index. 3) Publish minimal hermetic lint images per language (python, typescript, go, rust) built from a common, audited base and pinned by SHA; make these images immutable and consumed by lint jobs. 4) Integrate sccache/rust-cache and ccache hooks for compiled languages when materialized deps are used. 5) Add telemetry (cold vs warm durations, bytes mounted, registry calls, lint failures attributable to env drift). Rollout plan: start with a single service workspace (frontend-typescript) as a canary, then expand to backend-go and internal libs. Provide a fallback path that installs deps locally if remote mounting fails (graceful degrade). Acceptance criteria: - CI cold build time for canary reduced >= 35% compared to baseline - Lint job median time reduced >= 50% for canary - Registry calls for canary reduced >= 70% on cold runs - Hermetic lint images built and signed; lint job uses image by digest in 95%+ of runs - No increase in flakes attributable to materialization after two-week canary period
acceptance_criteria: Canary workspace cold build time reduced >= 35%
Registry calls for cold runs reduced >= 70%
Hermetic lint images published and pinned by digest
Fallback path triggers and completes within 3m when remote mount fails
Telemetry dashboard displays cold/warm separation and bytes mounted
risks: FUSE-based mounts may not be supported on all hosted CI executors; requires compatibility testing
Remote cache/CAS availability becomes a critical dependency; need SLOs and retries
Hermetic images must be frequently patched for CVEs; image maintenance overhead
Initial engineering effort might surface edge-case manifests for polyglot repos
implementation_notes: Spike showed a FUSE sparse materializer reduced npm cold install from ~3m to ~35s on the canary. Buildkit mount=type=cache approach is simpler for dockerized flows but lacks fine-grained remote index; we will support both and prefer the lighter-weight buildkit path for containerized jobs and FUSE for native language runners. Lint images target <250MB compressed; use multi-stage builds and strip docs. Use image signing via cosign and add verification step in CI runner init. Add feature flag remote-dep-mounting to toggle per-workspace. Metrics: ci.job.cold_duration, ci.job.warm_duration, ci.registry.calls, ci.bytes_mounted.
